title: Flood control back; House vows no ghost, substandard projects
summary: Despite the massive flak lawmakers have received, House leaders yesterday confirmed that flood control projects have been restored in the 2027 national budget and gave assurance there will be no…

blocks.text: November 26, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Despite the massive flak lawmakers have received, House leaders yesterday confirmed that flood control projects have been restored in the 2027 national budget and gave assurance there will be no irregularities.

Speaking on behalf of the House leadership, Deputy Speaker Janette Garin said flood control projects must continue to protect lives, livelihoods and the economy without compromising transparency and accountability.
“We believe that the House and the Senate will be united in our call for effective budget implementation – no substandard, no ghost and no overpriced projects,” Garin said yesterday.

The assurance came a day after the House approved on third and final reading House Bill 11602, or the proposed Metro Manila Flood Control and Drainage System Management Act, which would establish a unified flood control and drainage master plan for the metropolis.
Principally authored by Rep. Sandro Marcos, HB 11602 secured 212 affirmative votes, with no negative votes or abstentions.

Its passage came amid the restoration of P107.4 billion in proposed flood control funding under the Department of Public Works and Highways’ budget for fiscal year 2027, subject to final congressional approval.
More bills OKd

On Tuesday, the House approved several measures on third and final reading, including bills strengthening the Safe Spaces Act (or Bawal Bastos law) and lowering to 56 from 60 the retirement age of government personnel.

HB 10995’s proposed early optional retirement age aligns with the retirement age in the military, which is now 57 years, and in the Philippine National Police, which is 56 years for uniformed personnel.
HB 11264, meanwhile, imposes tougher penalties for gender-based sexual harassment and criminalizes grooming to better protect children from sexual abuse and exploitation.
Grooming is punishable by imprisonment or fines of up to P600,000, or both, regardless of whether the act leads to actual sexual abuse or exploitation, according to the bill.
Imprisonment shall be mandatory if the perpetrator is an adult and the victim is a child.
The measure imposes imprisonment or fines of up to P500,000, or both, for gender-based sexual harassment in workplaces and educational and training institutions.
Public officials and state workers who promote or encourage sexual harassment and misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic and sexist slurs will face stiff penalties.
First-time offenders face fines of up to P200,000 and mandatory suspension without pay for at least six months.
Repeat offenders face fines of up to P300,000, mandatory dismissal from office and disqualification from holding any public position for at least five years.

To combat online sexual harassment, the measure requires internet intermediaries to remove or block access to offending digital content within 24 hours of receiving a notice or lawful order from a competent authority.
Lower sodium

Health advocates and families of children with kidney disease have renewed calls for the passage of the Iwas Alat, Iwas Sakit bill requiring food manufacturers to gradually reduce sodium content in prepackaged products, citing the need to prevent chronic illnesses among Filipinos at an early age.

“Kidney health begins in childhood. By promoting healthy eating habits, reducing excessive sodium intake and encouraging healthier lifestyles early in life, we lay the foundation for preventing kidney disease and other chronic illnesses in adulthood,” said Johnny Tamon of the Philippine Society of Nephrology.

Kim Louise Areño, a registered nurse and representative of ImagineLaw, said educating children and their families about healthy lifestyles should be complemented by policies that improve access to healthier food products. — Christine Boton
